mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S600 V12 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M275 V12 for the S600 costs £7,500-£10,000 supply-only; a rebuilt M279 V12 costs £8,500-£12,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,500-£2,500 depending on complexity - V12 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of ignition coil failure on a Mercedes S600 V12?

acceptedAnswer.text: Misfires on multiple cylinders, rough running, and check engine lights are the classic warning signs on the M275 engine. The central voltage transformer and individual coil packs are a known weak point.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S600 V12 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M275 and M279 V12s are hand-built masterpieces, but they have known issues. The M275 is notorious for ignition coil and transformer failures, while the M279 can suffer from turbocharger and oil leak issues. With these addressed, both engines are fundamentally strong.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S600 V12 engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M275 and M279 V12 engines can reach 150,000+ miles, but ignition system and turbocharger issues typically require attention before then. One owner reported an M275 engine still running strong at 140,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S600 V12?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S600 is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M275 costs £7,500-£10,000 - significantly less than replacing a £8,000-£25,000 vehicle. For the W222 S600, the higher value (£20,000-£45,000) makes replacement even more justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S600 V12 need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M275 V12 requires approximately 10 litres; the M279 V12 requires approximately 11 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class S600 V12 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S600 V12 represents the pinnacle of Mercedes-Benz engineering - a hand-built twin-turbocharged V12 that has powered the flagship S-Class across three generations. The M275 5.5-litre biturbo V12 debuted in the W220 S600 in 2002, delivering effortless 493hp and 800Nm of torque. In 2006, the W221 S600 received a further-developed M275 producing 517hp. The M279 6.0-litre biturbo V12 succeeded it in 2014 for the W222 S600, producing 530hp. These engines represent the ultimate expression of Mercedes luxury and performance.

milestones.description: End of S600 production; V12 continues in Maybach S680

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class S600 V12 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The S600's M275 and M279 V12 engines are hand-built masterpieces, representing the pinnacle of Mercedes engineering. However, their complexity comes with significant maintenance challenges. Ignition system failures, turbocharger issues, and oil leaks are the most common problems driving replacement decisions. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M275 Ignition Coil & Voltage Transformer Failure
problems.h4: M275 Ignition Coil & Voltage Transformer Failure - The V12's Most Notorious Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M275's ignition system uses a central voltage transformer (sitting on top of the engine) that feeds 12 individual coil packs. The transformer can fail, leading to multiple cylinder misfires. Misfires on cylinders across both banks are a classic symptom.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace central ignition voltage transformer, clear fault codes
Replace transformer, all 12 coil packs, spark plugs, inspect wiring
Complete engine swap with new ignition components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If ignition failure has caused catalytic converter or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2002-2013 S600 V12 is worth approximately £8,000-£25,000 depending on generation, mileage and condition. These flagship saloons retain strong values for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a justifiable investment for owners of low-mileage or meticulously maintained cars.
problems.recommendation: M275 ignition issues are a notorious weakness. If you experience misfires, have the ignition system inspected immediately. Replacing the central voltage transformer at a specialist is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the failure has been prolonged, catalytic converter damage is possible - in which case a full rebuilt engine with new ignition components is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M275 Mercedes S600 V12 engine prices

problems.h4: M275/M279 Oil Leaks - The V12's Age-Related Issue
problems.rootCause: The M275 and M279 V12 engines are known for oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and oil pan seals. The sheer number of gaskets and seals on a V12 means more potential leak points.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets, clean oil seepage
repairOptions.longevity: If oil leaks are minor and localised

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets, oil pan gasket, camshaft seals
Complete engine swap with new gaskets and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical S600 V12 is worth £8,000-£25,000.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M275 and M279 are common with age but not usually urgent unless they are heavy. Valve cover gasket replacement at a specialist is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. Use only OEM Mercedes-Benz gaskets for these V12 engines - aftermarket seals are not recommended.

problems.h4: M279 Turbocharger & Cooling System Issues - The Modern V12's Weaknesses
problems.rootCause: The M279's twin-turbochargers can suffer from bearing wear, oil starvation, or actuator failure. Cooling system failures, including water pump and thermostat issues, have also been documented.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Visual inspection of turbochargers, oil supply lines, boost pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether turbo or another component is the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty turbocharger(s), oil feed lines, gaskets
Replace water pump, thermostat, coolant hoses, flush system
repairOptions.longevity: If cooling system failure is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with new turbos and cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo or cooling failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2014-2020 S600 V12 is worth approximately £20,000-£45,000 depending on mileage and condition. These ultra-premium flagships retain strong values, making replacement cost justifiable for well-maintained examples.
problems.recommendation: If you notice a loss of power, unusual turbo noises, or overheating on your S600, have the turbos and cooling system inspected immediately. Specialist turbocharger replacement is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. On an S600 worth £20,000-£45,000, preventative maintenance is always the better investment.

problems.rootCause: The V12's complex electrical systems, including ignition coils, ECU, and sensors, can fail. M279 engines use dual coil technology, which is more reliable than the M275's voltage transformer system, but failures still occur.
